verdict.outcome_basis: readout: "Independent Data Monitoring Committee has recommended to discontinue the trial as Epanova is unlikely to demonstrate a benefit to patients" (announcement:strength)

report.headline: The STRENGTH trial of omega-3-carboxylic acids (Epanova) 4 g/day versus corn oil placebo was stopped early for futility, and no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change was measured to enable causal effect estimation.
report.summary: STRENGTH randomized approximately 13,078–13,086 statin-treated patients with hypertriglyceridemia (TG 175–499 mg/dL) and low HDL to Epanova 4 g/day or corn oil placebo, targeting 1,600 MACE events over a planned 3–5 year follow-up (median 3 years per design). The independent data monitoring committee recommended discontinuation in January 2020 because Epanova was unlikely to demonstrate benefit. The causal calculator returned 'not_computable' with category 'insufficient_data' because no placebo-adjusted triglyceride reduction was measured in the STRENGTH population: phase 2 data showed only a within-arm −26% TG change (not placebo-adjusted), and phase 3 biomarker data at 3 g/day were not reported. The minimum detectable hazard ratio at 80% power was 0.869. Confidence is high that the fundamental limitation is the absence of a measured, placebo-adjusted biomarker effect.
key_evidence: ~13,078 patients randomized (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02104817 STRENGTH); 13,086 patients (Assessment of omega-3 carboxylic acids in statin-treated patients with high levels of triglycerides and low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol: Rationale and design of the STRENGTH trial.); 13,086 patients (Update on Phase III STRENGTH trial for Epanova in mixed dyslipidaemia)

report.what_would_change_this: A placebo-adjusted triglyceride change from STRENGTH or a phase 2 trial with proper placebo control at the 4 g/day dose would enable causal effect estimation; the full event count and hazard ratio at stopping would clarify whether a real effect was below the detection threshold.
report.readthrough_note: The corn oil placebo (vs mineral oil in REDUCE-IT) and uncertain triglyceride causality limit read-through to other omega-3 or triglyceride-lowering programmes; future trials need placebo-adjusted biomarker data and careful placebo selection to isolate drug effects.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: Open Targets shows no genetic evidence for coronary artery disorder for the molecular target(s) of omega-3-carboxylic acids. Omega-3 fatty acids act through multiple mechanisms (triglyceride lowering, anti-inflammatory, membrane effects) without a single well-defined drug target; no genetic studies link a specific target to coronary disease, so causal status is uncertain.
mechanism.notes: STRENGTH (NCT02104817) tested omega-3-carboxylic acids (Epanova) 4 g/day vs corn oil placebo on background statin in ~13,086 patients with hypertriglyceridemia (TG 175-499 mg/dL) and low HDL. Trial stopped early for futility (2020-01-13) before reaching planned 1600 MACE events. No placebo-adjusted biomarker data from the outcome trial are available. The only on-treatment triglyceride reduction is a phase 2, non-placebo-adjusted -26% at 4 g OM-3CA (12 weeks). Baseline TG taken as lower entry threshold 175 mg/dL. No LDL-C, apoB, non-HDL-C, or Lp(a) changes reported. Median follow-up ~3 years per design. Observed HR not reported; press release states 'Epanova is unlikely to demonstrate a benefit'.

for.text: No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured for Epanova 4 g/day in the STRENGTH population. Phase 2 data (EFFECT I) shows -26% TG within-arm only, explicitly not placebo-adjusted. Phase 3 biomarker data at 3 g/d, 90 days states 'None not stated'.

Calculator returns 'not_computable' with category 'insufficient_data' and weakest_link 'triglycerides change not measured'. Expected HR, causal RRR, and power are all null. Notes state: 'no measured change in triglycerides or another sized lipid: the effect is unknown, not zero'.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted triglyceride change from STRENGTH trial or a phase 2 trial with proper placebo control at the 4 g/day dose.

for.text: Corn oil placebo used (vs mineral oil in REDUCE-IT). Corn oil may have adverse metabolic effects that could attenuate apparent treatment benefit.
Primary endpoint is a broad MACE composite including coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina — softer components that may dilute treatment effect on hard outcomes.
Trial stopped early for futility before reaching planned 1600 events (median follow-up 3 years vs planned 3-5 years), reducing power to detect a modest benefit.
Inclusion triglyceride threshold 175-499 mg/dL (vs REDUCE-IT 135-499 mg/dL with established CVD/diabetes), potentially enrolling a lower-risk population.

against.text: Design elements (statin background, high-risk population, MACE endpoint) are consistent with other cardiovascular outcome trials. IDMC stopping for futility suggests true lack of benefit rather than design flaw.

hypotheses.would_settle: Head-to-head comparison of corn oil vs mineral oil placebo effects; analysis of endpoint components; full event count at stopping.

for.text: Reference table lists triglycerides causality as 'uncertain' (not established causal like LDL-C/apoB). Target genetics for omega-3-carboxylic acids also 'uncertain' (no genetic evidence found).

against.text: Cannot be tested because no placebo-adjusted TG change was measured in STRENGTH. The drug may not have lowered TG in this population, or TG lowering may be causal but the achieved magnitude unknown.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted TG change from STRENGTH plus outcome data; Mendelian randomization evidence for TG causality.

for.text: Target genetics for omega-3-carboxylic acids listed as 'uncertain' with 'no genetic evidence found' for the target and coronary artery disorder.

against.text: Target causality is distinct from biomarker causality; omega-3 mechanisms are pleiotropic (membrane effects, inflammation, etc.). Lack of genetic evidence is not evidence against causality.

hypotheses.would_settle: Genetic validation studies of omega-3 fatty acid targets for cardiovascular disease.

for.text: Minimum detectable effect HR at 80% power = 0.869 (calculator). Trial powered for 1600 events but stopped early, further reducing detectable effect size.

against.text: Calculator could not estimate expected HR or causal RRR because no placebo-adjusted biomarker change exists. The effect is unknown, not zero. Without knowing the achieved TG reduction, we cannot determine if a real effect was below detection threshold.

hypotheses.would_settle: Placebo-adjusted TG change to estimate expected effect size via causal pathway; full event count and HR at stopping.

for.text: TG inclusion 175-499 mg/dL may include patients with lower absolute risk than REDUCE-IT (which required established CVD/diabetes plus TG 135-499 mg/dL).

against.text: Population was high-risk: statin-treated, hypertriglyceridemia, low HDL, high CV risk. ~13,000 patients randomized. No subgroup data available to test heterogeneity.

hypotheses.would_settle: Subgroup analysis by baseline TG, established CVD vs primary prevention, HDL levels.

for.text: Trial stopped early by IDMC for futility.

against.text: No safety signals reported in phase 2. IDMC stopping for futility is proper trial execution, not an execution failure.

hypotheses.would_settle: Full trial report with enrollment, adherence, dropout, and event adjudication details.

against.text: No safety signals reported in phase 2 (EFFECT I, ISRCTN96712688). Corn oil placebo may have adverse effects, but this would bias toward null, not harm from active drug.

hypotheses.would_settle: Full safety data from STRENGTH trial.

issues.issue: Calculator input includes a triglycerides change (-26%) explicitly marked as 'phase2_not_placebo_adjusted' from f_055846c61d587f. The calculator correctly returns 'not_computable' with weakest_link 'triglycerides change not measured', but the case presents this non-placebo-adjusted value as the primary biomarker input. Per method, only placebo-adjusted phase 2 change at the outcome-trial dose is acceptable for causal mapping. The EFFECT I trial (pmid:30197273) had a corn oil placebo arm; the placebo-adjusted TG difference for 4g OM-3CA vs corn oil at 12 weeks is missing from verified facts and must be retrieved.
issues.request: Search for placebo-adjusted triglyceride change (OM-3CA 4g vs corn oil) at 12 weeks in the EFFECT I trial (pmid:30197273) or related publications. If unavailable, explicitly state that no placebo-adjusted TG data exists for the 4g dose and the calculator input should reflect 'not measured' rather than a within-arm value.

issues.issue: No phase 3 biomarker data for STRENGTH is available in verified facts (f_4d0a2fafa128b4 reports 'None not stated' for a 3g/d, 90-day human RCT). The case should note this gap as a caveat (severity medium) but not drop the quantified phase 2 input if it becomes placebo-adjusted.
issues.request: Confirm whether STRENGTH trial publications (post-2020) report on-treatment lipid changes (TG, LDL-C, HDL-C) by treatment arm. Search terms: 'STRENGTH trial lipid changes', 'Epanova triglycerides corn oil placebo', 'NCT02104817 biomarker results'.

issues.issue: Minor discrepancy in n_randomized across sources: 13,078 (CTgov), 13,086 (pmid:30125052), 13,086 (announcement). The case should use a single value with a note.
issues.request: Standardize n_randomized to 13,086 (from the design paper pmid:30125052 and announcement) with a footnote about CTgov listing 13,078.

issues.issue: Multiple inclusion threshold values in facts: 180 mg/dL (f_01b774dba5a165), 100 mg/dL (f_b43d35fe805760), 175-499 mg/dL (f_e3ff0b15fb7650). The announcement (2020-01-13) likely reflects the final protocol.
issues.request: Use 175-499 mg/dL from the announcement (f_e3ff0b15fb7650) as the primary inclusion criterion, noting earlier design papers had different thresholds.

issues.issue: Hypotheses list 'biomarker_not_causal' as a secondary category, but the calculator's category is 'insufficient_data' with weakest_link 'triglycerides change not measured'. The departure_from_calculator field is null, which is correct since primary category matches, but the secondary categories extend beyond calculator output. This is acceptable for hypotheses but should be clearly framed as speculative given the missing placebo-adjusted data.
issues.request: In the final report, qualify 'biomarker_not_causal' and 'effect_too_small' as untestable without placebo-adjusted TG data. Emphasize that the fundamental limitation is 'insufficient_data' (no placebo-adjusted biomarker change).

issues.issue: The 'design_or_endpoint' hypothesis is well-supported (corn oil placebo, broad MACE, early stopping). However, the corn oil placebo effect on lipids during the trial is unknown from verified facts. This could be a confounder if corn oil altered TG or LDL-C in the control arm.
issues.request: Search for STRENGTH trial lipid results by arm (Epanova vs corn oil) to assess placebo arm lipid trajectory. Search terms: 'STRENGTH trial corn oil lipid changes', 'Epanova vs corn oil triglycerides LDL'.

issues.issue: Calculator input uses a within-arm (not placebo-adjusted) triglyceride change of -26% from phase 2 (EFFECT I, pmid:30197273). The automatic check flags this. For causal mapping, the accepted input is a placebo-adjusted phase 2 change at the outcome trial's dose. Since no placebo-adjusted value exists for OM-3CA 4 g/day, the input should be omitted or set to null with a clear note, not presented as a quantified input.
issues.request: Search for placebo-arm triglyceride data in EFFECT I (pmid:30197273) or any other phase 2 trial of OM-3CA 4 g/day with a proper placebo control. If none exists, remove the within-arm value from calculator inputs and document that no placebo-adjusted biomarker change is available.

issues.issue: Hypotheses list 'biomarker_not_causal' and 'target_not_causal' as secondary categories, but both are marked 'undetermined' and explicitly untestable without placebo-adjusted TG data. Listing them as secondary categories overstates their support; they should be framed as speculative caveats under 'insufficient_data'.
issues.request: Reclassify 'biomarker_not_causal' and 'target_not_causal' as notes under the primary 'insufficient_data' category rather than secondary categories. Keep 'design_or_endpoint' as the only evidence-supported secondary category.

issues.issue: Calculator input uses baseline TG = 175 mg/dL (from STRENGTH announcement lower bound) but the -26% change comes from EFFECT I phase 2 trial which likely had a different baseline TG. Percent change must be paired with its own trial's baseline for absolute change calculation.
issues.request: Verify the baseline triglyceride value in the EFFECT I trial (pmid:30197273) for the OM-3CA 4 g arm. If different from 175 mg/dL, either use the correct phase 2 baseline or omit the input since it is not placebo-adjusted anyway.

issues.issue: Multiple inclusion threshold values in verified facts: 180 mg/dL (f_01b774dba5a165), 100 mg/dL (f_b43d35fe805760), and 175-499 mg/dL (f_e3ff0b15fb7650). The announcement (2020-01-13) is the latest source and likely reflects the final protocol.
issues.request: Clarify in the report that the final protocol used TG 175-499 mg/dL per the 2020 announcement; note the earlier design paper cited varying thresholds.

issues.issue: n_randomized discrepancy: 13,078 (ClinicalTrials.gov) vs 13,086 (rationale/design paper and announcement). Minor but should be harmonized.
issues.request: Use 13,086 (from the peer-reviewed design paper and announcement) as the primary figure; note the ClinicalTrials.gov value as a minor discrepancy.

STRENGTH is a large-scale CV outcomes trial evaluating the effect of Epanova 4g daily compared to placebo (corn oil) on reducing the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients on optimal statin therapy with mixed dyslipidaemia and at high risk for CV disease.

facts.value: The study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (corn oil), parallel group design that will enroll approximately 13,000 patients with hypertriglyceridemia and low HDL and high risk for CVD to be randomized 1:1 to either corn oil + statin or Epanova + statin, once daily, for approximately 3-5 years as determined when the number of MACE outcomes is reached.
